extracted.intended_audience: USCIS and DHS privacy officials, system owners, legal counsel, immigration practitioners, and members of the public who submit comments or seek records
extracted.subtask_description: System of Records Notice (SORN) describing DHS/USCIS-007 Benefits Information System: its purposes, categories of records and individuals covered, authorities, routine uses (permissive disclosures), storage/retention, safeguards, and access/contest procedures. Intended to notify the public and comply with the Privacy Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: SYSTEM NAME AND NUMBER
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Homeland Security (DHS)/U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)-007 Benefits Information System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal identifier of the system of records being modified and reissued.

rubrics_metrics.name: SECURITY CLASSIFICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclassified and Classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that records in the system may be maintained in both unclassified and classified networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: SYSTEM LOCATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Records are maintained at the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Headquarters in Washington, DC, and DHS/USCIS service centers and domestic and international field offices. Records are also maintained in DHS/USCIS information technology (IT) systems (e.g., CLAIMS 3, ELIS, CAMINO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies physical and IT locations where records are stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: SYSTEM MANAGER(S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief, Immigration Records and Identity Services, Identity and Information Management Division (IIMD), fieldrequests@uscis.dhs.gov, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Department of Homeland Security, 20 Massachusetts Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20529.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates the official point of contact responsible for the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: AUTHORITY FOR MAINTENANCE OF THE SYSTEM
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 103 and 290 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, as amended (8 U.S.C. secs. 1103 and 1360), the regulations issued pursuant thereto; and Section 451 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (Pub. L. 107-296).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory authorities authorizing collection and maintenance of the records.

rubrics_metrics.name: PURPOSES OF THE SYSTEM
rubrics_metrics.description: To permit USCIS's collection, use, maintenance, dissemination, and storage of paper and electronic immigration-related request information, including case processing and decisional data; to assist in processing immigrant and nonimmigrant benefit requests from intake through final decision; determine status of pending requests; account for fees and refunds; conduct FOIA/Privacy Act searches; locate related files; and support monitoring employee performance and production reporting (including tracking workload/efficiency and providing statistical analyses to USCIS leadership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also enables electronic processing, administrative reporting, and replication of data on DHS networks for analysis and vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: CATEGORIES OF INDIVIDUALS COVERED BY THE SYSTEM
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes benefit requestors and beneficiaries, derivatives/family members, sponsors (e.g., employers), attorneys, prospective and current accredited representatives, interpreters, preparers, fee payers, physicians who conduct immigration medical exams, and obligors (surety) and their agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates who is within scope of records this SORN covers (excludes asylum, refugee, intercountry adoption per footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: CATEGORIES OF RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM (GENERAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records include identifying information (names, aliases, addresses), unique identifying numbers (A-number, SSN, USCIS Online Account Number, DUNS), dates of birth/death, nationality, country of residence, gender/sex, marital/military status, contact info, immigration status, publicly available social media and public-facing website information, form responses, government-issued IDs, notices and communications, type of benefit requested, signatures, fee payment info, audio-visual recordings, and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an extensive list; many items are elaborated in benefit-specific and role-specific subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: CATEGORIES OF RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM (BENEFIT-SPECIFIC AND SENSITIVE DATA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit-specific eligibility information may include arrival/departure info, immigration history, familial relationships, relationship practices (e.g., polygamy), personal background (e.g., criminal offenses, national security involvement), organization membership, health information (vaccinations, communicable diseases, mental/physical disorders), travel, education, employment, professional accreditation, financial information (credit scores, income, assets, debts), public benefit info, supporting docs (birth/marriage certificates, DNA results), physical description, case processing metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms inclusion of potentially sensitive categories; biometric/background check results removed here because covered under DHS/USCIS-018.

rubrics_metrics.name: RECORDS ABOUT SPONSORS, ATTORNEYS, PREPARERS, PHYSICIANS, OBLIGORS
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of sponsors, attorneys, preparers, physicians, and obligors are collected: e.g., names, addresses, IDs (bar numbers, license numbers), accreditation data, qualifications, work history, signatures, bond information, power of attorney, contact info, financial info, and organizational affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what non-requestor personnel records may contain and be used for case processing and adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: RECORD SOURCE CATEGORIES
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS/USCIS obtains records directly from the immigration requestor, Representative, Physician, Preparer, Interpreter, or obligor/agents; USCIS personnel may input information during processing; BIS also stores/uses information from many USCIS, DHS, and other federal agency SORNs (lists include Alien File, FDNS, ADIS, ICE systems, FBI systems, State passport/visa records, Treasury collections records, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies internal and external systems and parties that feed data into BIS and notes changes in included/excluded source systems (added DHS/USCIS-017 and -018; removed DHS/USCIS-002 and -003).

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE A: Disclosure to DOJ and Other Federal Agencies for Litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: To DOJ, including U.S. Attorney's Offices, or other federal agencies conducting litigation or proceedings before any court, adjudicative, or administrative body, when relevant or necessary to the litigation or proceeding and one of specified parties (DHS, DHS employee, or the United States) is a party or has an interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive disclosure for litigation-related needs where DHS or its employees or the U.S. are parties/interested.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE B: Disclosure to Congressional Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: To a congressional office from the record of an individual in response to an inquiry from that congressional office made at the request of the individual to whom the record pertains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits response to constituent inquiries routed through Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE C: Disclosure to NARA/GSA for Records Management Inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: To the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) or General Services Administration pursuant to records management inspections under 44 U.S.C. secs. 2904 and 2906.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits records management oversight and inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE D: Disclosure for Audit or Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: To an agency or organization for the purpose of performing audit or oversight operations as authorized by law, but only such information as is necessary and relevant to such audit or oversight function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits disclosure to the data necessary for the audit or oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE E: Disclosure in Response to Suspected/Confirmed Breach
rubrics_metrics.description: To appropriate agencies, entities, and persons when (1) DHS suspects or has confirmed a breach of the system; (2) DHS determines there is risk of harm to individuals, DHS, the Federal Government, or national security; and (3) disclosure is reasonably necessary to respond to or prevent/minimize/remedy such harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added/updated to comply with OMB Memorandum M-17-12; permits breach-response information sharing with entities helping to contain/mitigate breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE F: Disclosure to Another Federal Agency to Respond to/Prevent Harm from Breach
rubrics_metrics.description: To another federal agency or federal entity, when DHS determines that information is reasonably necessary to assist the recipient agency/entity in (1) responding to a suspected or confirmed breach or (2) preventing, minimizing, or remedying risk of harm resulting from a suspected/confirmed breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental breach-response sharing authority for federal partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE G: Disclosure to Law Enforcement & Investigative Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: To an appropriate federal, state, tribal, local, international, or foreign law enforcement agency or other appropriate authority charged with investigating or prosecuting a violation or enforcing a law, when a record indicates a violation or potential violation and such disclosure is proper and consistent with the official duties of the person making the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits sharing when records indicate legal violations; includes criminal, civil, regulatory matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE H: Disclosure to Contractors/Agents Performing Work for DHS
rubrics_metrics.description: To contractors and their agents, grantees, experts, consultants, and others performing or working on a contract, service, grant, cooperative agreement, or other assignment for DHS, when necessary to accomplish an agency function related to this system of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must be subject to same Privacy Act requirements and limitations on disclosure as DHS officers and employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE I: Disclosure to Clerks and Judges of Naturalization Courts
rubrics_metrics.description: To clerks and judges of courts exercising naturalization jurisdiction for the purpose of filing applications for naturalization and to enable such courts to determine eligibility for naturalization or grounds for revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates naturalization processes administered through courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE J: Disclosure to Department of State for Benefit Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Department of State for the purpose of assisting in the processing of benefit requests under the Immigration and Nationality Act, and all other immigration and nationality laws including treaties and reciprocal agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports interagency processing of immigration benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE K: Disclosure to Other Agencies During Investigations or Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: To appropriate federal, state, tribal, and local government law enforcement and regulatory agencies, foreign governments, and international organizations, as well as to other individuals and organizations during an investigation by DHS or the processing of a matter under DHS jurisdiction, or during a proceeding within immigration/nationality laws, when DHS deems disclosure necessary to carry out functions and statutory mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad authority for sharing in investigations and proceedings when necessary for DHS functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE L: Disclosure for Hiring/Retention/Security Clearances
rubrics_metrics.description: To an appropriate federal, state, local, tribal, foreign, or international agency, if the information is relevant and necessary to a requesting agency's decision concerning hiring/retention, issuance of security clearance, license, contract, grant, or other benefit; or to a DHS decision concerning similar personnel or contracting actions, when disclosure is appropriate to official duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits sharing to support personnel suitability, vetting, and benefit determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE M: Disclosure to OMB for Review of Private Relief Legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Office of Management and Budget in connection with the review of private relief legislation as set forth in OMB Circular No. A-19 at any stage of the legislative coordination and clearance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports legislative review processes requiring access to records.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE N: Disclosure to Attorney/Representative Acting for an Individual
rubrics_metrics.description: To an attorney or representative (as defined in 8 CFR 1.1(j)) who is acting on behalf of an individual covered by this system of records in connection with any proceeding before DHS/USCIS or DOJ EOIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits communications with legal representatives of affected individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE O: Disclosure to Agencies to Collect Debts/Erroneous Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To a federal, state, tribal, or local government agency to assist such agencies in collecting repayment of loans, fraudulently or erroneously secured benefits, grants, or other debts owed to them or to the U.S. Government, or to obtain information that may assist USCIS in collecting debts owed to the U.S. Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits cross-agency collaboration for debt collection and recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE P: Disclosure to Foreign Governments to Collect Debts
rubrics_metrics.description: To a foreign government to assist such government in collecting repayment of loans, fraudulently or erroneously secured benefits, grants, or other debts owed to it, provided the foreign government (1) provides sufficient documentation to establish validity of purpose and (2) provides similar information to the U.S. upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional sharing with foreign governments for debt collection subject to reciprocity and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE Q: Disclosure to Coroners for Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: To a coroner for purposes of affirmatively identifying a deceased individual (whether or not deceased as a result of a crime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted sharing for death identification purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE R: Disclosure to HHS/CDC/State Local Health Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with INA, to HHS, CDC, or any state/local health authorities to (1) provide proper medical oversight of DHS-designated civil surgeons performing medical examinations and (2) ensure health issues affecting public health and safety are being or have been adequately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports public health oversight and coordination regarding immigration medical exams and public health threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE S: Disclosure to Agencies Verifying Citizenship/Immigration Status
rubrics_metrics.description: To a federal, state, or local government agency seeking to verify/ascertain the citizenship or immigration status of any individual within the jurisdiction of the agency for any purpose authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits status verification for authorized purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE T: Disclosure to SSA for Issuing SSN and Card
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Social Security Administration for the purpose of issuing a Social Security number and card to an alien who has made a request for a SSN as part of the immigration process and in accordance with related agreements and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports issuance of SSNs tied to immigration processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE U: Disclosure to Former Employees for Official Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: To a former employee of DHS, in accordance with applicable regulations, for purposes of responding to an official inquiry by a government entity or professional licensing authority or facilitating communications when Department requires information or consultation assistance from the former employee regarding a matter within that person's former area of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits contacting/former employees for operational or personnel-related purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE V: Disclosure to Prospective/Current Employers
rubrics_metrics.description: To an individual's prospective or current employer to the extent necessary to determine employment eligibility (e.g., pursuant to Form I-140) or, USCIS may share information with petitioning employers to aid in the approval or denial of a request to become a permanent resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited employer access for adjudication or employment-eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE W: Disclosure for Intelligence/Counterintelligence/Antiterrorism
rubrics_metrics.description: To a federal, state, or local agency, or other appropriate entities or through established liaison channels to selected foreign governments, in order to provide intelligence, counterintelligence, or other information for intelligence, counterintelligence, or antiterrorism activities authorized by U.S. law or Executive Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits sharing for national security and counterterrorism activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE X: Disclosure to Approved Benefit-Granting Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: To approved federal, state, and local government agencies that grant public benefits, licenses, grants, governmental credentials, or for any other statutorily authorized purpose when immigration status of the benefit applicant is legally required and an approved Memorandum of Agreement or Computer Matching Agreement is in place between DHS and the entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional sharing to agencies for entitlement or licensing when legal and agreement prerequisites are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE Y: Disclosure to Department of Labor for Labor Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Department of Labor for enforcement of labor certification violations and violations of U.S. labor laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits labor law enforcement coordination and investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE Z: Disclosure to News Media/Public During Naturalization Ceremonies
rubrics_metrics.description: To the news media and the public during the course of naturalization ceremonies administered by USCIS or a Federal Judge. Pursuant to 8 CFR 337.2 individuals to be naturalized are generally required to appear in a public ceremony, unless specifically excused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits release of information related to public naturalization ceremonies; updated to replace 'Immigration Judge' with 'Federal Judge' in Routine Use Z text elsewhere in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE AA: Disclosure to Department of Treasury for Payment Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: To the Department of Treasury to perform initial processing of benefit requests and to accept and resolve payment and any related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates financial processing and payment resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE BB: Disclosure to Government Agencies for Testing New Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: To appropriate federal, state, local, tribal, or foreign governmental agencies or multilateral governmental organizations, with the approval of the Chief Privacy Officer, when DHS is aware of a need to use relevant data that relate to the purpose(s) stated in this SORN, for purposes of testing new technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New routine use allowing sharing for authorized technology testing with privacy office approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE CC: Disclosure to Benefit-Granting Agencies to Ascertain Public Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To federal, state, local, and tribal benefit granting agencies (e.g., Social Security, housing, food, unemployment) to ascertain whether public benefits have been issued to the immigration requestor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits verification of public benefits receipt by benefit requestors.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE DD: Disclosure to Bond-Posting Individuals/Entities
rubrics_metrics.description: To an individual or entity seeking to post or arrange, or who has already posted or arranged, an immigration bond for an alien, to aid the individual or entity in (1) identifying the location of the alien; (2) posting the bond; (3) obtaining payments related to the bond; or (4) conducting other administrative or financial management activities related to the bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports bond posting and associated administrative/financial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE EE: Disclosure of Petition Outcomes to Consulting Entities/Labor Unions
rubrics_metrics.description: To a consulting entity (e.g., a labor organization or management organization) that provided an advisory opinion on a petition to USCIS seeking O or P nonimmigrant classification. USCIS may disclose the outcome of the petition to the consulting entity that provided an advisory opinion on the petition. USCIS may disclose petition outcomes to labor unions in instances in which USCIS approves or denies a petition submitted with a union consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits feedback to consulting entities and unions that participated in advisory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUTINE USE FF: Disclosure to News Media/Public with Chief Privacy Officer Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: To the news media and the public, with the approval of the Chief Privacy Officer in consultation with counsel, when there exists a legitimate public interest in disclosure; when disclosure is necessary to preserve confidence in the integrity of DHS; or when disclosure is necessary to demonstrate accountability of DHS's officers, employees, or individuals covered by the system, except where release would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional public/media disclosure for legitimate public interest, accountability, or integrity purposes with privacy office and counsel approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: INFORMATION SHARING FOR DEBT COLLECTION (ICE Financial Operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with DHS's information sharing mission, BIS information may be shared with other DHS components that need it, including sharing with DHS's U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Financial Operations—Burlington regarding fees charged during immigration request processes to ensure collection of debts; BIS information may also be shared with credit reporting agencies via ICE Financial Operations—Burlington.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a particular operational sharing relationship to support debt collection and credit reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: POLICIES AND PRACTICES FOR STORAGE OF RECORDS
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS/USCIS stores records electronically or on paper in secure facilities (e.g., locked drawers/behind locked doors); records may also be stored on magnetic disc, tape, and digital media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General statement of physical and electronic storage practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: POLICIES AND PRACTICES FOR RETRIEVAL OF RECORDS
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS/USCIS may retrieve records by using any of the data elements listed (e.g., name, date of birth, Alien Number, SSN, USCIS Online Account Number, Receipt Number) or combinations thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes retrieval keys and methods used to find records in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: POLICIES AND PRACTICES FOR RETENTION AND DISPOSAL OF RECORDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Each form type is governed by a respective retention schedule dictated by USCIS's final action (approved, denied, abandoned, withdrawn, administratively closed, rejected). Alien File records are permanent; DHS/USCIS may transfer Alien Files to NARA 100 years after individual's birth. Case management systems retain records per NARA-approved schedules generally between 25-50 years from last completed action. Electronic notices/communications retained for 13 years after last action. Records of electronic appointments maintained for 60 days. Daily reports retained per general retention schedules. Replicated records on DHS networks follow same retention schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention varies by form type and action; rationale includes law enforcement, FOIA/Privacy Act, national security, and ability to respond to follow-up inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADMINISTRATIVE, TECHNICAL, AND PHYSICAL SAFEGUARDS
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS/USCIS safeguards records according to applicable rules and policies, including DHS automated systems security and access policies. USCIS has imposed strict controls to minimize risk of compromise. Access limited to individuals with a need to know and appropriate clearances/permissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes access controls and security measures to protect data confidentiality and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: RECORD ACCESS PROCEDURES
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals seeking access or notification of records or seeking to contest content may submit a request in writing or electronically to the Chief Privacy Officer or USCIS's FOIA Officer (contact via http://www.dhs.gov/foia). Requests must conform with Privacy Act regulations (6 CFR part 5), verify identity (full name, current address, date/place of birth), be signed and notarized or submitted under 28 U.S.C. 1746, and should explain why the Department would have the information, identify components that may have the information, specify when records were created, and provide other helpful info. Requests for another living individual's records must include that individual's certification consenting to access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains identity verification, required content of requests, possible use of FOIA even when Privacy Act/JRA do not provide access rights, and contact resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONTESTING RECORD PROCEDURES
rubrics_metrics.description: For records covered by the Privacy Act or covered JRA records, follow 'Record Access Procedures' above. Any individual, regardless of immigration status, may file a FOIA request. Throughout benefit determination and prior to denial, USCIS provides individuals opportunity to address and correct information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives procedural assurances for dispute/correction opportunities and FOIA alternative when Privacy Act access is limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOTIFICATION PROCEDURES
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'Record Access Procedures' above for notification procedures (i.e., how individuals are notified and can request/verify records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification follows same procedures as access and contesting; identity verification requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: EXEMPTIONS PROMULGATED FOR THE SYSTEM
rubrics_metrics.description: None. However, when this system receives a record from another system exempted under 5 U.S.C. 552a, DHS will claim the same exemptions for those records that are claimed for the original primary systems of records from which they originated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No system-specific exemptions, but inherit exemptions from source systems where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBLIC COMMENTS: SUBMISSION DEADLINE AND METHODS
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments on or before November 12, 2019. Methods: Federal e-Rulemaking Portal (http://www.regulations.gov) following submission instructions; Fax to 202-343-4010; Mail to Jonathan R. Cantor, Acting Chief Privacy Officer, Privacy Office, DHS, Washington, DC 20528-0655. All submissions must include agency name and docket number DHS-2019-0042.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how to submit comments, the docket number, and required inclusion of identifying docket info for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PUBLIC COMMENTS: POSTING AND REDACTION
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received will be posted without change to http://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided. Agencies review submissions and may redact or withhold certain submissions or portions thereof; submitted comments may not be available to read until agency approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns commenters that personal data will be posted and that agencies may redact or withhold information.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOCUMENT IDENTIFIERS, DATES, AND AVAILABILITY OF OFFICIAL PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: This document published as FR Doc. 2019-22156 (84 FR 54622) with pages 54622-54629 and effective/other dates noted. The XML rendition is not the official edition; users should use the linked PDF on govinfo.gov for the official electronic format. The prototype FederalRegister.gov is unofficial and does not provide legal notice until ACFR designates it official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains official publication status and where to verify authoritative content (PDF on govinfo.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: HISTORY / PRIOR SORNS AND FOOTNOTES
rubrics_metrics.description: References to prior related Federal Register notices (e.g., 81 FR 72069 (Oct 19, 2016); 73 FR 56596 (Sep 29, 2008)) and footnotes clarifying scope (e.g., this SORN does not cover asylum, refugee, intercountry adoption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical context and scope exceptions via footnotes.
